title: The one cross term the fourth power of a sum does not kill
statement: Let Y be a family of rational-valued random variables on a finite index range [0, n) with weights p, and let z be any further rational-valued variable on the same range. If for every pair of distinct indices i, i' below m the mixed expectation E[Y_i Y_i' z^2] vanishes, then the expectation of the square of the pointwise sum of the first m, times z^2, is the sum over i < m of E[Y_i^2 z^2]. The off-diagonal pairs die and the diagonal survives; that surviving diagonal is the only term the multinomial expansion of a fourth power does not kill under four-wise uncorrelatedness. The pairing hypothesis is spelled out rather than packaged as Rat.FourwiseUncorrelated because the induction runs over m while z is a variable OUTSIDE that range -- in the intended use it is Y_m itself -- so the hypothesis must be uniform in m, and this one is.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.expectation_sq_sumVars_mul_sq : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Rat))) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Rat)) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> Rat)) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : ((x5 : AxNat) -> ((x6 : AxNat) -> ((x7 : AxNat.lt x5 x4) -> ((x8 : AxNat.lt x6 x4) -> ((x9 : Not (Eq.{1} AxNat x5 x6)) -> Eq.{1} Rat (Rat.expectation (fun (x10 : AxNat) => Rat.mul (x0 x5 x10) (Rat.mul (x0 x6 x10) (Rat.mul (x1 x10) (x1 x10)))) x2 x3) Rat.zero)))))) -> Eq.{1} Rat (Rat.expectation (fun (x6 : AxNat) => Rat.mul (Rat.mul (Rat.sumVars x0 x4 x6) (Rat.sumVars x0 x4 x6)) (Rat.mul (x1 x6) (x1 x6))) x2 x3) (Rat.sumRange (fun (x6 : AxNat) => Rat.expectation (fun (x7 : AxNat) => Rat.mul (Rat.mul (x0 x6 x7) (x0 x6 x7)) (Rat.mul (x1 x7) (x1 x7))) x2 x3) x4)))))))

evidence.supports: The declaration is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with an empty Kernel::axiom_footprint, together with every other ADR-1653 declaration. The test asserts Environment::contains FIRST, because an absent name has an empty footprint too.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib rat_prelude::fourth_moment::fourth_moment_tests::fourth_moment_declarations_are_axiom_free -- --exact 2>&1 | grep -c '^test result: ok. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: grep -c, not grep -q: -q would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail, and -c exits 1 printing 0 when the line is absent, so a suite that compiled to zero tests and exited 0 is caught rather than counted as a pass. --release is mandatory: the rational prelude SIGABRTs on the default debug thread stack.

notes: Proved by its own induction rather than by two applications of the sumVars-peeling lemma plus a delta collapse. Rat.sumRange_delta is unusable here: its hypothesis is UNRESTRICTED (for all t, t != i implies f t = 0) while four-wise uncorrelatedness supplies zeros only below the bound. The successor step instead splits the square by a ring identity and kills the middle term with Rat.expectation_sumVars_mul_eq_zero, so the diagonal is never separated from a rectangle at all. A bounded sumRange_delta_lt would be a genuine addition to rat_prelude/sum.rs; it was not needed once this induction existed, and that is a note rather than a claim.
